title: Vaineau, Barachant & Andreev 2013 — Brain Invaders Adaptive versus Non-Adaptive P300 Brain-Computer Interface dataset (BI2013a)
description: EEG recordings from 24 healthy participants performing a visual P300 Brain-Computer Interface task using the Brain Invaders video game, collected at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, in 2013. The experiment compares a P300-based BCI with and without adaptive calibration using Riemannian geometry. Each participant completed multiple sessions with randomized adaptive and non-adaptive runs, recorded with 16 wet electrodes at 512 Hz.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a g.USBamp amplifier (16 Ag/AgCl electrodes, g.GAMMAcap, 512 Hz, left earlobe reference, ground at FZ) using OpenViBE. Each session had two runs (Non-Adaptive and Adaptive, randomized order), each with a Training phase (80 Target and 400 non-Target flashes) and an Online phase. In the Non-Adaptive run the Training data calibrated an MDM classifier. In the Adaptive run the classifier was initialized with generic class geometric means and continuously adapted using a Riemannian method. The interface had 36 symbols in 12 groups, and subjects were blind to the mode of operation.
